Flow Angles Defines the flow direction as the composition of rotations of a unit Reference Vector around certain axes of a reference Coordinate System . These rotations are known as Euler angles. When you set Method to Constant , set Value to the φ , θ , ψ rotations. When Method is Field Function , set Angles Function to an appropriate function. You can also provide tables. Three different rotation conventions are supported to define the coordinate axes that are used, and the order in which the rotations apply. Choose a Rotation Convention as follows: X Convention (Z-X-Z) : For Euler angles ( φ , θ , ψ ), the first rotation is by angle φ about the z-axis, the second is by angle θ about the x-axis, and the third is by angle ψ about the z-axis. Y Convention (Z-Y-Z) : For Euler angles ( φ , θ , ψ ), the first rotation is by angle φ about the z-axis, the second is by angle θ about the y-axis, and the third is by angle ψ about the z-axis. Yaw, Pitch, Roll Convention (Z-Y-X) : For Euler angles ( φ , θ , ψ ), the first rotation is by angle φ about the z-axis, the second is by angle θ about the y-axis, and the third is by angle ψ about the x-axis. To set the backflow pressure, the following options are available: Environmental —subtracts the dynamic head at the boundary. This approach discourages backflow from occurring. Static —does not use the dynamic head. The pressure is maintained at the specified pressure. Blocked reverse flow —sets the boundary flux to zero and subtracts the dynamic head at the boundary. This approach stops the backflow from occurring and encourages the fluid to start flowing outwards. The backflow static temperature is set explicitly. Pressure Constraints Simcenter STAR-CCM+ provides a range of options for constraining the pressure on the boundary: Non-Reflecting —prevents spurious numerical reflection of the solution into the solution domain. Unsteady Non-Reflecting —prevents spurious acoustic reflections in unsteady, compressible, and non-isothermal simulations. Target Mass Flow —automatically applies a correction to the specified pressure boundary value in an attempt to yield the specified mass flow rate. Pressure Jump —imposes a pressure rise or pressure loss at the boundary obtained from a specified fan curve, a porous inertial/viscous resistance, or a pressure loss coefficient. Average Pressure —adjusts the pressure profile from the cells next to the pressure outlet boundary so that the average of that profile is equal to the average pressure value specified. This adjusted profile is then applied to the faces of the pressure outlet boundary. For turbomachinery simulations, a Radial Equilibrium boundary condition is available. It represents the difference between the absolute pressure and the reference pressure. In flows without the influence of gravity, the working pressure is equal to the static gauge pressure. If the gravity model is active, the working pressure is equal to the piezometric pressure, as shown in Eqn. (738) for variable and constant density flows. When a turbulence model is used, the working pressure implicitly includes the contribution of 2 3 ρ k . However, this contribution can be considered negligible in most flows of engineering interest. GUID-72EFFF8B-9297-4715-95AC-2E94852D8D7.text: CCM+ provides the following options to control how the pressure is calculated when backflow occurs across the boundary: Environmental —by default, the dynamic head at the pressure outlet boundary is subtracted in the case of inflow. Static —select this option to maintain the specified pressure at the boundary and do not use the dynamic head. Blocked reverse flow —select this option if you expect only transitory backflow across the boundary in the course of the simulation. Simcenter STAR-CCM+ sets the boundary flux to zero and subtracts the dynamic head for all reversed flow faces at the boundary. You are advised to select this method only if you do not expect reversed flow at the pressure outlet boundary to occur at the end of the simulation when a steady simulation has converged or an unsteady simulation has reached the statistically converged regime. If you use this method for situations where there is reversed flow at the pressure outlet boundary at convergence, you can obtain unphysical results. For compressible and non-isothermal flows, to prevent spurious numerical reflection of the solution into the solution domain: Select the Physics Conditions > Pressure Outlet Option node and set Option to Non-Reflecting or Unsteady Non-Reflecting for steady or unsteady simulations, respectively. Note that these options are only available when you use the Coupled Flow model. Select the Physics Values > Non-Reflection Mode Specification and set the Number of modes to retain. Specify a number of modes that is less than the number of cells in the circumferential direction. For more information, see Flow Boundaries Reference—Pressure Outlet .
